Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
933 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes were made to the forecast this morning.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry and warm conditions expected through the end of the week.

- 2) Increasing confidence in a low pressure system impacting our
  region Sunday into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and warm conditions expected through the end of
the week.

High pressure approaching from the central CONUS will build
overhead today and shift offshore through Saturday. This will
yield well above average temperatures over the next several days
along with very dry air. Plenty of sunshine each day with 
highs approaching the middle to upper 60s to near 70 by Friday 
across the region. Lows at night will remain in the 30s to 40s 
through the week. One caveat to the prolonged dry conditions and
warming temperatures could have implications on fire weather (see
Fire Weather section below). 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Increasing confidence in a low pressure system 
impacting our region Sunday into Monday.

This week's persistent upper-level ridge will gradually start to 
slide offshore late this week between Friday and Saturday, as a 
second ridge looks to continue building over the Northeast over the 
next several days. This will result in continued dry conditions 
through the start of the weekend, with temperatures ranging well 
above normal. 

As we look towards late in the weekend into next week, model runs 
have now been consistently showing a shortwave disturbance forming 
over the Southeast near the Florida peninsula that could begin to 
traverse north late this weekend into early next week. Model runs 
continue to show large uncertainty in where exactly this low will 
end up, but several ensemble and ML outputs show increasing 
precipitation chances across the Mid-Atlantic beginning late Sunday 
& into Monday. A large amount of this uncertainty is a result of a 
potent upper-level trough forming over the western half of CONUS and 
tracking east in the same time period, which will significantly 
influence where this southeastern low ends up. Model guidance on 
this trough is still all over the place, so will continue to monitor 
as guidance gets a better handle on how these synoptic pieces will 
interact. Regardless, it does seem that the potential is increasing 
for cloudier, wetter weather overall early next week.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions are anticipated through Sunday afternoon as dry 
conditions persist. Light winds generally flow NW Friday before 
shifting easterly Saturday.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds stay below SCA thresholds through Sunday, but could start to 
increase late Sunday night ahead of an incoming low pressure system. 
Winds shift easterly on Saturday before shifting northerly
Sunday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
High pressure will move directly overhead today and remain there
over the next few days. Expect warming temperatures and very dry
air to take hold as a result. While winds will remain low, RH 
values will go down substantially. Overnight recoveries, 
especially on the ridges, will be very poor as well starting 
tonight. Expect afternoon RH values to drop well into the teens 
and 20s each day west of the Blue Ridge, and the 20s to 30s east 
of the Blue Ridge. This will also be paired with seasonably warm 
temperatures, so this will really act to dry out already very dry 
fuels. While fire will be slow to move due to lack of wind, very
dry air will make for easy fire starts, so exercise extreme
caution in the coming days. 

Not helping matters is that there is no precipitation expected 
east of the Appalachians through at least the end of the week. 
Given the setup, will really be watching for any potential dry 
frontal passages in the long range as the next days to really 
watch out for. Still watching late weekend into early next week 
for the next weather system, but unsure what it will bring at this
point. While precipitation chances have increased a bit over the
past several days, it is still not a certainty by any means. 
Should the areas miss out on substantial precipitation from this
system, there could be some fire weather concerns early next
week with dry frontal passage. Continue to monitor the latest 
forecast as this timeframe approaches.
